reviewer: Benchmark author; condition visible; qualitative audit, not independent clinical review
scope: 12 prespecified outputs: four held-out cases at seed 17 across basic, context, and review
summary: The smaller Qwen2.5 model frequently returned fenced JSON or malformed/overlong content. Among parseable examples, it repeated cards, exceeded word limits, and sometimes converted missing information into claims. The review prompt did not repair these issues in the inspected examples.

entries.finding: Returned fenced JSON rather than the requested bare object. All six cards were long adult-directed questions, exceeded the three-word limit, and introduced unsupported claims about Tara reading or seeking help.
Same content as basic despite added context. Cards were overlong adult-directed questions and repeated unsupported assumptions about reading and help-seeking.
Review repeated the context draft unchanged. It preserved the JSON fence, role mismatch, unsupported assumptions, and word-limit violations.
Parseable six-card object, but cards repeat several facts, include an unnecessary allergy statement, and exceed the three-word limit. No repair of the missing preference is attempted.
Added context produced a more task-specific sandwich suggestion, but cards still exceed the three-word limit and repeat facts rather than offer concise optional choices.
Review was identical to context. It did not shorten cards or resolve repeated and unsupported content.
Returned fenced JSON with repeated cards, long adult-style prompts, and invented first-person story content. The three-word limit was not followed.
Cards remained overlong and included unsupported claims such as a friendly fox and a curious child. Added context did not make the output concise.
Review exactly repeated context output, including unsupported traits and word-limit violations.
Cards were mostly grounded but overlong for the three-word limit, repeated water facts, and used adult first-person wording rather than short optional communication cards.
Context output was identical in substance to basic. It retained repeated cards and word-limit violations.
Review did not repair the draft; it repeated the same overlong, repetitive cards.
